subject: Banking
title: Washington Mutual: Largest Bank Failure Ever
description: A quick, practical guide to Washington Mutual: Largest Bank Failure Ever.

hook.text: Washington Mutual was the largest bank failure in US history. $307 billion in assets collapsed in September 2008.

buildup.text: WaMu aggressively sold subprime mortgages. Loan officers were paid bonuses based on volume, not quality.

discovery.text: Depositors withdrew $16.7 billion in 10 days. The FDIC seized the bank and sold it to JPMorgan for $1.9 billion.

twist.text: WaMu's CEO Kerry Killinger received $25 million in compensation the year before the bank failed.

climax.text: WaMu proved that volume-based lending incentives create fraud. When you pay for quantity, quality disappears.

punchline.text: $307 billion gone. The CEO earned $25 million the year before collapse.

quiz.question: What made Washington Mutual's lending so risky?
options: Loan officers were paid bonuses based on volume, not quality

details.summary: Washington Mutual was the largest bank failure in US history when the FDIC seized it in September 2008 with $307 billion in assets. JPMorgan bought its deposits and branches for $1.9 billion, wiping out shareholders and bondholders.
details.whyItMatters: WaMu's failure demonstrated that even the largest thrift institution in America could be destroyed by reckless mortgage lending. Its orderly resolution showed that the FDIC could manage even massive failures without direct taxpayer cost.
takeaways: WaMu had $307 billion in assets, making it the largest US bank failure
The bank lost $16.7 billion in deposits in the 10 days before seizure
JPMorgan acquired the banking operations for $1.9 billion

faq.question: What caused Washington Mutual to fail?
faq.answer: WaMu had aggressively expanded subprime mortgage lending and held billions in risky option ARM loans. When the housing market collapsed, loan losses consumed the bank's capital. A classic bank run in September 2008 sealed its fate.

faq.question: Why did WaMu's failure not cost taxpayers money?
faq.answer: The FDIC sold WaMu's banking operations to JPMorgan, which assumed the deposits and took on the assets. Shareholders and unsecured bondholders were wiped out, absorbing the losses instead of taxpayers. The FDIC fund was not depleted.
